clue.text: Young animals surrounding the woman's children

indicators.note: the young animals are placed all around the woman's word, enclosing it

parts.note: cubs are the young of bears, lions and foxes
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A mother animal's cubs gather around another woman's offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are angelic infants, and the word is used affectionately for sweet small kids.

clue.text: Trouble at bath time?

parts.note: a fix you are in is idiomatically described the same way as what fills the tub

explanation.definitionFit: Being in hot water is the idiom for being in trouble, and bath water is literally hot.

clue.text: Dependable engineers exposed to risk

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
liable means open or subject to something unwelcome

explanation.surface: Trustworthy engineers who are nevertheless vulnerable to danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something you can depend upon is trustworthy and consistent.

clue.text: Want followers to support bishop and reprobate

indicators.note: in a down clue the later pieces sit beneath the bishop, holding it up

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
want in the sense of need or shortage is lack
sheep are proverbial for following the crowd

explanation.surface: A church needs followers to back its bishop and deal with a sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A black sheep is the disreputable member of a family or group, a scoundrel.

clue.text: Great and good present during most of dinner, for example

indicators.note: the letter for good is there in the middle of the trimmed meal
the last letter is dropped, leaving most of the word

parts.note: dinner is one example of a meal

explanation.surface: Something great and good is on offer through most of a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims MEAL to MEA, and G goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for huge or excellent, a synonym of great.

clue.text: Judy's fella keeps a spare tyre

indicators.note: the puppet's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: Punch is Judy's husband in the traditional British Punch and Judy puppet show

explanation.surface: Judy's husband holds on to a spare car tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a seaside puppet show in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is British slang for a roll of fat round the waist, a pot belly.

clue.text: Moneyspinner for accountant caught in exhibition

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: the cricket letter for caught is placed inside the word for exhibition

parts.note: a show is a public exhibition
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An accountant is caught out at an exhibition making money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably generates profit.

clue.text: Terrible catastrophe with no char for them!

definitions.text: Terrible catastrophe with no char for them!

indicators.note: terrible signals the letters of catastrophe are jumbled, minus the letters of char

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Imagine the disaster of having no tea to put in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C, H, A, R from CATASTROPHE ('with no char') and rearrange the remaining ATSTOPE. Char is British slang for tea, so the whole clue also describes the objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots for brewing tea would face disaster if there were no tea at all.

clue.text: Primates back charge for divorce

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for primates in reverse

parts.note: apes are primates
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: Monkeys and apes pay a fee for their divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: As verbs, to divorce and to part or split up mean the same.

clue.text: Fantastic rates negotiated to include students

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the students inside them
negotiated suggests the letters of rates being worked over into a new order

parts.note: L is a learner driver, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: Excellent rates have been agreed that cover students too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiated' reads like rates being agreed, but it is the anagram signal giving STEAR, which 'to include' wraps around LL (two learner drivers).
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar is informal for outstanding, from its sense of starry.

clue.text: Part of high street with redeeming features?

definitions.text: Part of high street with redeeming features?

parts.words: Part of high street with redeeming features?
parts.note: a shop where pledged goods are redeemed for cash, punning on redeeming features as good qualities

explanation.definitionFit: Pawnbrokers' shops sit on high streets, and owners redeem pledged items there.

clue.text: Turn sanctimonious student out of gambling game

parts.note: pi is British informal for sanctimonious, short for pious

indicators.note: the student letter is removed from the gambling game

parts.note: roulette is a casino gambling game
L is a learner, hence a student

explanation.surface: A self-righteous student turns away from a gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes L from ROULETTE to leave ROUETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a spin on one foot in ballet, a kind of turn.

clue.text: Block request for material

parts.note: to dam a river is to block it
ask means request

explanation.surface: Someone asks for material to block a request.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a patterned woven fabric, traditionally silk or linen.

clue.text: Condition making a horse trot strangely

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the phrase appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A horse's odd trotting points to a health problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful throat is a medical complaint or ailment.

clue.text: Attachments to hips given by tense excited doctor

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
high means elated or excited
Bones is slang for a doctor, from sawbones and the Star Trek medic

explanation.surface: A nervous, agitated doctor hands over hip attachments.
explanation.definitionFit: Femurs join the pelvis at the hip joint, so they are attached there.

clue.text: Duck out of quite a lot

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words quite a lot

explanation.surface: Ducking out of a great deal of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal is a small freshwater species of dabbling duck.

clue.text: Former English beauty accommodating five administrators

definitions.note: plural here, as the body of managers is a collective singular noun

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the word for beauty takes in the Roman numeral for five

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive person
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An ex-English beauty queen puts up five managers.
explanation.definitionFit: The executive is the collective name for an organisation's senior managers.

clue.text: Regret returning to refreshing air in monied area

indicators.note: returning says the word for regret is read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret
ozone is popularly used for fresh, bracing seaside air

explanation.surface: Feeling remorse when going back to the fresh air of a wealthy district.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro area is a currency zone, a region defined by its money.

clue.text: One small island in the Med attached to Germany, but separate

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
I is one in Roman numerals
Crete is a large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A small Mediterranean island linked to Germany yet apart from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means distinct or individually separate, unlike its homophone meaning tactful.

clue.text: Climber's requirement that is full of cold cream

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is holds the letter for cold

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
C is cold, as on taps
the cream or pick is the best of a group

explanation.surface: A mountaineer needs the item that is full of chilled cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers use a small axe-like tool to cut steps in ice.

clue.text: Nation's bank rapidly emptied

parts.note: to bank on is to count on, so bank and count both mean rely

indicators.note: emptied removes all the inner letters of rapidly, leaving the outside pair

explanation.surface: A country's bank is quickly cleaned out of funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nation is a country with its own people and government.

clue.text: A French and Italian fighting force

parts.note: un is the French for a
It is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A Franco-Italian army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a sub-division of an army, a group of soldiers.

clue.text: One who's never happy to go over temporary repair

parts.note: to cross is to go over
a patch is a quick, makeshift fix

explanation.surface: A grumpy person going over to a temporary repair job.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspatch is an informal word for a grumpy, bad-tempered person.

clue.text: Piano frequently imported by Stallone

indicators.note: the word for frequently is brought into the actor's first name

parts.note: Sylvester Stallone is known as Sly
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: A piano is often shipped in by Sylvester Stallone.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano is the musical direction for playing quietly.

clue.text: Start to speak about black freshwater fish

parts.note: B is black, as in pencil grades
the roach is a European freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Beginning a conversation about a dark river fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for discussion.

clue.text: Fashion fair open — it gives coverage for clothes

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so these letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: At an open fashion fair, an item provides cover for outfits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is an apron-like garment worn to protect the clothes beneath.

clue.text: Criminal executed for swindle

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter of the criminal is lopped off

parts.note: a crook is a criminal

explanation.surface: A criminal is put to death for fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' cuts off the head (first letter) of CROOK.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook someone is old slang for cheating or defrauding them.

clue.text: PA system initially failing, Milliband is peeved

indicators.note: the first letter of the PA system goes missing

parts.note: Tannoy is a British brand name for a public address system
Ed Miliband is a British Labour politician

explanation.surface: Ed Miliband is annoyed when the PA system fails at the start of his speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially failing' drops the T from TANNOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: peeved and irritated both describe mild vexation.

clue.text: Runs into weird local in 'Ring O'Bells'

indicators.note: the letter for runs goes inside the rearranged letters
weird says the letters of local in come out oddly arranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a strange local inside the Ring O'Bells pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' turns LOCAL IN into CAILLON, and 'into' places R after its first two letters. The Ring O'Bells is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillon is a set of tuned bells rung together, so a ring of bells.

clue.text: American communist accepting he is led

parts.note: a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: An American communist allows he is being guided.
explanation.definitionFit: To usher someone is to show or lead them somewhere.
